subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: What does activity do for my body, and how do I judge my own effort?

prompts.prompt: Name the movement cues for what the heart and lungs do during activity and explain what each one does.
Show, describe, or diagram noticing my own effort level. A demonstration, a spoken description, and a drawing are equally valid.
Apply muscular strength and endurance activities in a new movement task at a challenge level you select. Control and cue use are assessed, not speed, distance, or count.
A made-up learner is struggling with flexibility and mobility. Identify the likely cue or decision at fault, correct it, and explain why the correction helps.
Connect what the heart and lungs do during activity with enjoying activity every day. Explain how one supports the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Assemble a personal activity circuit you enjoy, with an easier and a harder option for each station, and explain how you judge your own effort.
Describe one way you adapted a task so it worked for you, and one activity from this unit you would choose to do again. There is no wrong answer here.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
